_meta.notes: Tailoring playbooks for engineering and science_pharma (research/placement-year/07 §6), same contract as tailor-playbooks-tech-product.json: guidance for reordering, emphasis and equivalent-term substitution only; never add facts, numbers, tools, employers or escalate authorship. Quotes were checked against the page or PDF text on the accessed date.

sources.title: How to write the perfect engineering CV and cover letter
STEM Placements and Internships CV Example
Sample CV: Biomedical Sciences with Industrial Placement
12 Month University Industrial Placement Student (UIPS): Analytical Chemistry

recruiterScan: Technical skills block: are the advert's CAD, analysis and programming tools visible and grouped?
One design, build or test project with the student's own role, the method and a technical result.
leadWith: The bullet naming the advert's tool or method (SolidWorks, FEA, MATLAB, PLC).
Test, simulation or performance results already on the CV, with units.
The component or subsystem the student owned.
Safety, standards or quality actions already shown.
engineering.summaryFormula: Only when the CV already has a profile: shorten it to at most two lines of facts it already states (degree, year, discipline, and the tools or projects the bullets already show). Leave out any job title the student is applying for and the grade. If the CV has no profile, leave it out: never write one.

reframes.from: did the CAD for the project
reframes.onlyIf: the component and the tool are named in the CV
the CV says it was FEA and names the part
the student's own part is stated
the sub-team and task are stated; keep member, never upgrade to lead
the part and the machine are named

reframes.to: Student member, Institution of Mechanical Engineers
reframes.onlyIf: always: never write MIMechE or CEng for a student

sectionOrder: Education (degree, relevant modules with marks, design project)
pitfalls: Software-style framing (tech stack, GitHub) for a mechanical role.
Tool lists with no project context.
Jargon without a plain-English purpose line.

evidence.claim: recruiterScan: modules most relevant to the role
evidence.quote: list the modules you have taken that are most relevant to the role you are applying to.

evidence.claim: recruiterScan: group projects and dissertation in Education
evidence.quote: information on group projects and your dissertation, any modules relevant to the job, and relevant academic awards

evidence.claim: recruiterScan/leadWith: named tools and practical skills
evidence.quote: Subject specific technical knowledge: SolidWorks, AutoCAD, SolidCam, CNC Machining; milling, facing, drilling, and turning

evidence.claim: leadWith/reframes: tool and method named in the project bullet
evidence.quote: Carried out FEA (Finite Element Analysis) in SolidWorks to analyse the stresses
demonstrate your technical, engineering design, and manufacturing skills
important lessons on team working, time management, project management, budgeting and presentation
These titles may only be used by individuals with current Engineering Council registration.
explaining technical information to non-technical colleagues

recruiterScan: Named lab techniques matching the advert, with where they were used.
A lab project with its aim, method, result or mark.
Protocol and data discipline (SOPs, lab notebook, GLP or GMP if real).
leadWith: The bullet naming the advert's technique (HPLC, PCR, cell culture).
Lab results already on the CV (yield, purity, samples run).
science_pharma.summaryFormula: Only when the CV already has a profile: shorten it to at most two lines of facts it already states (degree, year, subject, and the techniques the bullets already show). Leave out any job title the student is applying for and the grade. If the CV has no profile, leave it out: never write one.

avoid: Assisted with (unless the original says so)
Discovered (unless it was a genuine finding)

reframes.onlyIf: the techniques are named in the CV
where it was used is stated

reframes.from: final year project in organic chemistry
reframes.onlyIf: the aim and at least one technique are stated

reframes.to: followed written SOPs and kept a lab notebook
reframes.onlyIf: the CV says protocols or a notebook were used; never write GLP or GMP for a teaching lab
the poster was presented at a named event

reframes.to: Student member, Royal Society of Chemistry
reframes.onlyIf: always: never write MRSC or CChem for a student

sectionOrder: Education (degree, relevant modules with marks, lab project)
pitfalls: Academic-CV framing (publications first) for an industry placement.

evidence.claim: recruiterScan/leadWith: named techniques that match the advert
evidence.quote: chromatographic (HPLC, GC, CE, SFC), spectroscopic (NMR UV, FTIR)
Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP), Good Laboratory Practice (GLP)

evidence.claim: recruiterScan: techniques grouped in a lab skills line
evidence.quote: Developed practical lab skills including DNA extraction, PCR, ELISA & Gel electrophoresis.
The report received a grade of 64%.

evidence.claim: reframes: poster at a named module or event
evidence.quote: Produced an academic poster communicating research findings from the Energy for Life module.
IT skills – competent user of Microsoft Office, Matlab and SPSS
